what: Round 1218. What a video review changes in top division football, per match, as published counts. The Club Manager review rates are DERIVED from this file by scripts/genCmVarRates.mjs. Nobody types a rate.
rules: A FIGURE is one quantity in one competition in one season. A figure is USED only when at least two independent publishers, on two hosts, each made their own count of it. A figure with one publisher is THIN: it is on file and it is not used, not for a target and not for a range.

Where the two publishers of a figure count differently, both counts are on file and the engine takes the STRICTER one, the lower count. Among the used figures of a quantity the target is the lowest per match figure, so a review moves fewer results, never more. Nothing is averaged.
The range of a quantity runs from the lowest to the highest count among its USED figures. scripts/simCmVar.mjs holds the engine inside that range plus headroom it measured.
A count is copied as the page prints it, with the sentence or line it was read from. Matches a season is arithmetic on the league's size (20 clubs: 380, 18 clubs: 306).

What the lead asked for and the pages do not give is written under owed, with what was looked for. While an owed entry is open the switch CM_VAR_LIVE stays false: scripts/simCmVarLedger.mjs fails otherwise.

goalsRuledOut.label: goals ruled out after a review, per match

penaltiesAwarded.label: penalties awarded after a review, per match

penaltiesCancelled.label: penalties cancelled after a review, per match
penaltiesCancelled.why: The engine never takes a given penalty back. Recorded so the number is on file when it does.

goalsAwarded.label: goals awarded after a review, per match
goalsAwarded.why: The engine has no goal that was first flagged off and then given.

redCards.label: red cards after a review, per match
redCards.why: The engine reviews goals and penalties only.

reviewsRejected.label: reviews after which the referee kept the call, per match
reviewsRejected.why: One publisher, and it does not say whether the call was a goal, a penalty or a card. So the game never shows a review that ends with the call standing.

awardedPenaltiesScored.label: penalties awarded after a review that were scored
awardedPenaltiesScored.why: One publisher. A penalty a review awards is taken under the engine's own penalty kick law (the base rate a shootout kick uses), not under a number of its own.

owed.rule: The lead's decision 1 of Round 1218 asks for each number on two independent publishers for at least two recent seasons.
owed.found: The one season counted by two publishers is Serie A 2017-18, that league's first season under review. Every count of a season from 2022-23 on that three readers found on 2026-10-10 (Premier League, La Liga, Serie A, Bundesliga, Ligue 1) is one publisher's own, or one newspaper's count repeated by other sites. The recent counts on file, each THIN: goals ruled out 0.124 to 0.145 a match (the used figure, 0.076, is lower, so the game rules out fewer goals than those seasons did), penalties awarded 0.066 to 0.131 a match (the used figure, 0.089, sits inside that).
owed.closes: Add a second publisher's own count for two seasons from 2022-23 on, or the lead accepts the rates as sourced: set state to accepted and write the ruling (who, when, in what words) under ruling. Then run node scripts/genCmVarRates.mjs.

notUsed: Why a goal is ruled out (offside, handball, a foul) is split by one publisher only (the ESPN rows above). THIN: the review card names no reason.

La Liga 2024-25: one newspaper's count (Diario AS: 189 interventions, 86 penalties, 40 goals ruled out for offside) repeated by other sites, for one https://www.goal.com/en-ke/lists/shocking-stats-reveal-real-madrid-most-penalised-var-barcelona-lead-favorable-calls/blte3296d088f740c2d . One publisher, and the copies do not agree on what the 86 counts. Not a row.

Totals of interventions with no split (the Dutch and the German federations' season figures, the Brazilian league's 2025 survey) say nothing about goals or penalties. Not rows. Their urls were not kept when they were read, so a reader cannot open them from here.
